aria: Animated recap of the Hawks' 117 to 112 win over the Thunder: Aaron Wiggins' 3-pointer with 2.2 seconds left before halftime, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Onyeka Okongwu's 28 points and five threes, the top scorers, how the Hawks won, and Friday's game against Charlotte.
notes: Box score from the Hawks' 117–112 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder at Paycom Center on Nov 18, 2026, from the BasketUSA box score, checked against the Associated Press story (via Yahoo Sports and News 9), OKC Thunder Wire (via Yahoo Sports), Atlanta News First and theScore's line score and team stats. All 117 Atlanta points and all 112 Oklahoma City points are accounted for in the player lines, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Atlanta 31–29 after one, 64–51 at the half, 83–83 after three, 34–29 in the fourth. Team stats (threes 20 of 50 to 9 of 27, offensive rebounds 14–5, steals 8–5, assists 32–30, blocks 4–9) are from the box score and match theScore except for Oklahoma City's three-point attempts (theScore and Thunder Wire say 26). Atlanta's biggest lead (13) is from Peachtree Hoops (via Yahoo Sports) and BasketUSA; no source gives Oklahoma City's biggest lead, so it is left off. Atlanta News First lists Okongwu with 27; the box score and AP give 28. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Atlanta led 64–51 at the half on Wiggins' 3 with 2.2 seconds left (AP). Oklahoma City won the third 32–19 and tied it 83–83 on Ajay Mitchell's driving layup with 1.4 seconds left in the quarter (AP). Threes by Dort and Wiggins gave Atlanta a 92–86 lead it never gave up, and Zuby Ejiofor's 3 made it 102–92 (AP). Okongwu had 18 in the first half (AP); Jalen Johnson had a triple-double, 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists (AP; Atlanta News First). Dort and Wiggins, traded from the Thunder this summer, got video tributes in their first games back (AP). It was Oklahoma City's first home loss of the season (Field Level Media; Atlanta News First). The Thunder played without Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren and Kingston Flemings (AP). Atlanta hosts Charlotte on Friday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Aaron Wiggins' 3-pointer with 2.2 seconds left before halftime that gave Atlanta a 64–51 lead (AP gives the clock and the score). The recaps don't describe the shot further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The later threes that put Atlanta ahead for good are described without a clock, so they are not drawn. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Atlanta Hawks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wiggins' listed 6-foot-5 and 190 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-9¾ wingspan measured at the 2021 NBA Draft Combine (NBADraft.net), in the Hawks' road colors. No source confirmed his Hawks number, so his jersey has no number. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
